summary: Phase 4 Composio→Missions wiring tested via /app/backend/tests/test_composio_phase4_missions.py (17/17 pytest cases pass). Covers: build_composio_mission_tools short-circuits (Tool=None / is_available()=False / 0 ACTIVE connections / lead-agent tools_enabled=False), happy-path Tool() shape (monkeypatched composio.get_tools_for_user → returns 2 Tool instances with name='gmail.send_email'/'slack.post_message', description prefixed with [toolkit], handler callable, side_effect=True), budget arithmetic (per-platform cap trips at 5, total cap trips at 20, reset_budget clears counters), mission regression (POST /api/orgs/{org}/missions w/ no connections returns 200 + mission persists + status 'running'), Phase 1+2+3 routes untouched (toolkits/agent-tool-prefs/connect-bad-toolkit all return expected codes), slug helpers (_short_name and _slug_for round-trip correctly). FOUND ONE CRITICAL BUG: composio_mission_tools.py line ~165 calls db.llm_calls.update_one(..., sort=[('created_at', -1)]) but pymongo 4.5.0 (installed) does NOT accept the sort kwarg on update_one — sort=... was only added in pymongo 4.7+. Every successful Composio tool call inside a mission will raise TypeError at telemetry write-time. Verified by direct repro in test_update_one_sort_kwarg_incompatible_with_pymongo_4_5; same code path without sort= works fine (test_update_one_works_without_sort_kwarg).

critical.issue: db.llm_calls.update_one(..., sort=[('created_at', -1)]) raises TypeError on pymongo 4.5.0 — sort kwarg was only added in pymongo 4.7+. Every successful Composio mission tool call will throw after execute_tool succeeds, breaking telemetry and surfacing a noisy error in mission logs (the surrounding try/except in _augment is at build-time, not handler-time, so the exception bubbles up into run_mission_loop's tool dispatch).

minor.issue: _bump_budget is only called on res.get('success') — failed Composio calls don't count toward the cap. A perpetually-failing toolkit (e.g. expired auth) could be retried indefinitely by the LLM with no budget pressure to back off.

reset_budget(mission_id) is called on every invocation, including resume/rehydrate paths — accumulated counters from the first half of the mission are wiped when the loop re-enters. Probably intentional (fresh budget per loop entry), but worth a comment.

The update filter is {org_id, kind_label='composio:<tk>:<slug>'} with no user_id and (broken) sort. Two users in the same org running missions with the same toolkit can race; the broken sort was supposed to pick the latest, but without it the filter would update an arbitrary historical row. Recommend filtering on user_id as well (or just write a NEW telemetry row instead of mutating chat rows).

action_items: FIX (CRITICAL): /app/backend/composio_mission_tools.py line ~165–172. Either (a) switch to db.llm_calls.find_one_and_update(filter, update, sort=[...]) which accepts sort on pymongo 4.5+, OR (b) drop the sort=... kwarg and accept that multi-call races may update an older row, OR (c) bump pymongo to >=4.7 in /app/backend/requirements.txt. Option (a) is the cleanest match for the original intent.
Consider: bump _bump_budget on every execute regardless of success, so failed-auth toolkits get back-pressure (currently only successful calls count toward the 20/5 caps).
Consider: filter telemetry update on user_id in addition to org_id+kind_label to avoid cross-user row mutations under concurrent mission load.
critical_code_review_comments: Gating chain (Tool=None / is_available() / 0 ACTIVE / tools_enabled=False) is correctly ordered cheapest-first — DB hit only after the in-memory checks pass.
_short_name('LINEAR') → 'linear' (single-token fallback) handles non-canonical slugs without crashing; matches the _slug_for inverse on the round-trip.
_summarise() correctly clips at 5 properties and prioritises required fields when packing the args_hint sample — keeps the catalog block under control even for tools with 30+ params.
description gets truncated at 240 chars w/ an ellipsis BEFORE the [toolkit] prefix is added, so the prefix never gets clipped — good ordering.

_BUDGETS as a process-global dict is fine for a single backend worker, but if the deployment ever scales to multiple uvicorn workers (>1), the per-mission counter splits — different workers will each track their own copy and the 20/5 caps become per-worker not per-mission. The doc comment acknowledges 'partial count is moot anyway on crash' but multi-worker is a different failure mode. Worth a note.

_augment_with_composio_tools (missions.py L2070) takes a `tools` arg but the inner build_composio_mission_tools ignores it — only the returned `extra` list is concatenated. The arg is purely for the convenience of `list(tools) + list(extra)`. Slightly redundant; build_composio_mission_tools could just return the new list.
Mission start flow at missions.py:515 wraps the augment in try/except — good defensive posture given Composio API can be flaky.

rca of the issue: RCA for the pymongo update_one(sort=...) bug: pymongo's update_one signature is (filter, update, upsert=False, bypass_document_validation=False, collation=None, array_filters=None, hint=None, session=None, let=None, comment=None) in 4.5.0; the sort kwarg only landed in 4.7 (Apr 2024). The intent of the code is correct — when a user invokes a Composio tool from inside chat, an llm_calls row is recorded with kind_label='composio:gmail:GMAIL_SEND_EMAIL' (chat shape), and when the same call is then invoked from a mission's tool catalog, the handler should re-tag the most recent matching row with the mission_tool: prefix. The sort=[('created_at', -1)] is to grab the most recent. The fix is to use find_one_and_update which DOES accept sort in all pymongo versions: result = await db.llm_calls.find_one_and_update({org_id, kind_label}, {'$set': {...}}, sort=[('created_at', -1)]). Reproduction: insert one llm_calls doc with kind_label='composio:gmail:GMAIL_SEND_EMAIL' then call db.llm_calls.update_one(..., sort=[('created_at', -1)]) → TypeError: Collection.update_one() got an unexpected keyword argument 'sort'.
